ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=CB$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $F$ is a point on the extension of $AB$, and point $E$ is on $BC$, with $BE=BF$. $\triangle ABE \cong \triangle CBF$. If $\angle CAE = 20^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle ACF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB=BC$ and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle CAB=\angle ACB=45^\circ$. Also, given that $\angle BAE=\angle CAB-\angle CAE=45^\circ-20^\circ=25^\circ$ and according to (1), $\triangle ABE\cong \triangle CBF$. Hence, $\angle BCF=\angle BAE=25^\circ$, which means $\angle ACF=\angle BCF+\angle ACB=45^\circ+25^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

Therefore, $\angle ACF=\angle BCF+\angle ACB=25^\circ+45^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, F, B, A are on the same horizontal straight line, F is to the left of B, and A is to the right of B; C is directly above B, CB is a vertical line segment, and E is located on line segment CB; connect C to F and A respectively, and connect E to A. It can be seen from the figure that at point C, ray CB is between ray CA and ray CF. Reasoning: Given AB=CB and ∠ABC=90°, △ABC is an isosceles right triangle, so ∠BAC=∠ACB=45°. In the figure, AE is inside ∠BAC, and it is given that ∠CAE=20°, therefore ∠BAE=∠BAC-∠CAE=45°-20°=25°. Also given △ABE≅△CBF, according to the correspondence A↔C, B↔B, E↔F, the corresponding angles ∠BAE=∠BCF can be obtained, so ∠BCF=25°. Since in the figure CB is between CA and CF, ∠ACF=∠ACB+∠BCF=45°+25°=70°.
